newsitem.title: USA: Perot spent lightly in failed presidential bid.
newsitem.headline: Perot spent lightly in failed presidential bid.

text.p: Texas billionaire Ross Perot may have suffered a crushing defeat in this year's presidential election, but at least it didn't cost him much.

Perot, who spent almost $70 million of his own money in his 1992 bid for the White House, this year shelled out less than $1,500 up to and including Nov. 25, officials of his Reform Party said Thursday.

Campaign manager Russ Verney said the party detailed the spending in documents to the Federal Election Commission last week, but added that more bills were still coming in and that Perot may have to pick up some of them.

While Perot ran entirely on his own money in 1992, this year he received slightly more than $29 million in federal funds. By accepting those funds, Perot was restricted to spending no more than $50,000 from his personal fortune.
But the feisty businessman did spend about $8 million from his own pocket in setting up the Reform Party and getting it on the ballot across the country.
Perot won 19 percent of the vote in 1992 but scored just 8 percent this time around. He is estimated to be worth about $3.3 billion.
